issues.legal_issue: An assembly that begins lawfully may become an unlawful assembly when its members respond to a call to assault a person, even without prior concert.
material_facts: The courts found that the accused arrived with a large group of labourers and armed men while paddy was being cut.
When the complainant came to protest, one accused called for an assault and the others chased him in response.
The courts below had not established which side possessed the disputed land.
issues.conclusion: The assembly became unlawful when the members responded to the call and chased the complainant; prior concert was not required.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 141 of the Indian Penal Code, including its Explanation, an assembly lawful at its inception may subsequently become unlawful, and previous concert is unnecessary. The common object under Section 141 differs from the common intention under Section 34. An unlawful act by one or two members does not change the character of an assembly if the others do not acquiesce. The Court relied on the statement of the principle in Ratanlal's Law of Crimes.

rule.if: criminal_conviction_appeal and assembly_gathered_for_another_purpose and member_called_for_assault and members_chased_in_response and victim_was_assaulted

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal from a criminal conviction.
predicates.assembly_gathered_for_another_purpose: A group assembled for a purpose other than assaulting the victim.
predicates.member_called_for_assault: A member of the group called for the victim to be assaulted.
predicates.members_chased_in_response: Other members chased the victim in response to that call.
predicates.victim_was_assaulted: The victim was assaulted by members of the group.

issues.definition: When a group assembled for another purpose has a member call for an assault, other members chase the victim in response, and the victim is assaulted, the assembly becomes unlawful even if it was initially lawful.

issues.legal_issue: An imperfect charge that combines distinct objects of an assembly does not invalidate a conviction when the defect causes no prejudice.
material_facts: The charge described theft of paddy and assault on the complainant as objects of the assembly without setting them out separately.
The accused were acquitted of the theft-related charge because possession was not proved.
The first information report described the facts in detail, and the case involved a small number of accused and witnesses who gave concise accounts.
The Court found that no one could have been misled by the way the objects were stated.
issues.conclusion: The defect in the charge was curable and did not require the convictions to be set aside because no prejudice was shown.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 225 and 537 of the Code of Criminal Procedure make an irregularity in a charge curable where it has not occasioned prejudice. Distinct objects stated in one charge are not necessarily inseparable, and an imperfection alone does not invalidate a conviction.

rule.if: criminal_conviction_appeal and charge_combined_distinct_objects and charge_was_imperfect and case_facts_were_disclosed and no_prejudice_was_caused

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal from a criminal conviction.
predicates.charge_combined_distinct_objects: The charge stated distinct objects of the assembly together rather than separately.
predicates.charge_was_imperfect: The way the charge was framed contained an irregularity.
predicates.case_facts_were_disclosed: The prosecution's account of the material facts was disclosed to the accused.
predicates.no_prejudice_was_caused: The defect did not mislead or otherwise prejudice the accused.

issues.definition: If an imperfect charge combines distinct objects but the case facts were disclosed and the defect caused no prejudice, the conviction is not set aside for that irregularity.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction based on witness credibility is not disturbed on appeal when the challenge concerns only the credibility of witnesses whom the courts below believed.
material_facts: One accused was convicted for his individual act of using a spear to injure the complainant.
The challenge to that conviction concerned the credibility of the witnesses who testified to the act.
The witnesses had been believed by the courts below.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to interfere with that conviction and dismissed that part of the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied its usual rule of not interfering on questions of fact, including a challenge confined to the credibility of witnesses believed by the courts below.

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal from a criminal conviction.
predicates.challenge_only_concerns_witness_credibil: The appellant's challenge to the conviction concerns only whether the witnesses were credible.
predicates.courts_below_believed_witnesses: The courts below accepted the testimony of the witnesses in question.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges only the credibility of witnesses whom the courts below believed, the appellate court does not interfere with the factual conviction.

issues.legal_issue: A member of an unlawful assembly who is armed with and uses a spear may be convicted under the provision governing rioting while armed with a deadly weapon.
material_facts: The assembly became unlawful when members chased the complainant in response to a call for assault.
One accused was armed with a spear and used it to injure the complainant.
issues.conclusion: The conviction under Section 148 of the Indian Penal Code was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Section 148 of the Indian Penal Code applies to rioting by a person armed with a deadly weapon. Once the assembly was unlawful, the accused's being armed with and using a spear brought his case within that section.

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal from a criminal conviction.
predicates.person_was_member_of_unlawful_assembly: The person was a member of an unlawful assembly that engaged in rioting.
predicates.person_was_armed_with_deadly_weapon: The person was armed with a deadly weapon while participating in the rioting.

issues.definition: When a person who was armed with a deadly weapon participated in rioting as a member of an unlawful assembly, the armed-rioting conviction is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A sentence for rioting and assault does not warrant appellate leniency where a large armed group attacks an unarmed person peacefully protesting after seeking official assistance.
material_facts: The accused arrived with a group that included numerous armed men while paddy was being cut.
The complainant went to the police and returned with police personnel before protesting at the scene.
The complainant was unarmed, and members of the group assaulted him.
The Court found that the circumstances did not call for leniency.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to interfere with the sentences.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed whether the circumstances warranted appellate interference with the sentences, taking into account the presence of a substantial armed group and the attack on an unarmed person who had sought assistance from the authorities.

rule.if: criminal_sentence_appeal and large_armed_group_present and victim_was_unarmed_and_protesting and victim_sought_official_assistance and group_attacked_victim

predicates.criminal_sentence_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal seeking interference with a criminal sentence.
predicates.large_armed_group_present: A large group that included armed persons was present at the scene.
predicates.victim_was_unarmed_and_protesting: The victim was unarmed and peacefully protesting.
predicates.victim_sought_official_assistance: The victim sought assistance from the authorities before protesting at the scene.
predicates.group_attacked_victim: Members of the group attacked the victim.

issues.definition: When a large armed group attacks an unarmed person who is peacefully protesting after seeking official assistance, the sentence is not reduced on appeal.
